subject: NovusHealth: bundled onboarding + custom FHIR adapter — exec approval request
messages:
From: Sam Jackson <sam.jackson@novushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com, Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@novushealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-01 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — onboarding + integration

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the proposal. We're generally happy with the pricing and timeline, but our CTO flagged one item that will change scope materially: Novus requires a custom FHIR adapter to map our internal resource extensions (patient.mrn_extension and encounter.site_code) to the model pipeline. That work wasn't in the original SOW.

Can Redwood absorb the engineering effort as part of the bundled onboarding (we were counting on the premium onboarding package covering integration), or do we need a separate work order? If it is additional, we'll need an estimate and a reconciliation on pricing and SLA (we need a 99.9% uptime target for inference endpoints).

I've attached a short document outlining the FHIR mappings we need and our initial acceptance criteria. We'll need to finalize this by next week to hit our go-live target.

Sam
Procurement & Integrations
NovusHealth

Attachments: integration_requirements.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jackson <sam.jackson@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — onboarding + integration

Sam — thanks for the detail and for the doc. Appreciate the clarity on the extensions.

Short answer: the premium onboarding package covers integration adapters that map standard FHIR resources, but custom resource extensions are out-of-scope and typically quoted as an additional engineering engagement. That said, Novus is a priority account for this quarter and we want to avoid blocking your go-live.

I've attached the current SOW and our pricing schedule for transparency. I'll escalate internally for an exception request to cover the FHIR adapter under the existing bundle and to confirm the 99.9% inference SLA (that SLA is higher than our standard premium support; it will require a Dedicated capacity commitment or an SLA amendment).

Next steps:
- I'll loop in Marcus (CS Lead) and request exec-level approval for a one-time engineering concession + SLA amendment.
- Can you confirm whether Novus can commit to the Dedicated pool if we add the SLA? That will materially affect pricing.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: SOW_Novus_v1.pdf, pricing_schedule.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-02 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval needed: NovusHealth — include custom FHIR adapter in onboarding bundle

Team — flagging for quick review. NovusHealth (ND-2027-1107) is asking that we include a custom FHIR adapter for two internal resource extensions as part of the premium onboarding bundle. Details: attached.

Why this matters:
- Business: $425k ARR net-new annual commitment if we keep them on Hosted + Dedicated burst capacity.
- Timeline: they need the integration done in ~3 weeks to hit their clinical trial launch.
- Risk: the adapter is non-trivial (estimated 2-3 engineer-weeks) and requires end-to-end validation with their dev/staging environment.

Requesting approval for a one-time concession:
- Roll forward the onboarding bundle to include up to 3 engineer-weeks of custom integration work at a capped internal cost (we'd not bill Novus separately).
- Offer the 99.9% inference SLA if Novus signs up for Dedicated for the initial 3-month period (we can re-evaluate after month 3).
- Approve a 10% discount on the first-year support fee to compensate for the concession.

Attachments: SOW_Novus_v1.pdf, integration_requirements.docx

Marcus — can you confirm technical effort/impact? Vivek — need your sign-off on the concession and SLA amendment (or guidance on alternate routing to Product/Legal).

Best,
Kimberly
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-03 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec approval needed: NovusHealth — include custom FHIR adapter in onboarding bundle

Thanks for the write-up — read quickly with Marcus. I agree to the proposed one-time concession under the following guardrails:

1) Cap the engineering concession at 3 SFEs (staff-field-equivalent) / 120 hours total; any overage requires explicit approval from me and Product.
2) Offer the 99.9% inference SLA only if Novus commits to a minimum 3-month Dedicated reservation at the proposed committed throughput (documented in the SOW). After month 3 we will review telemetry and decide whether to continue or convert to Hosted with a different SLA.
3) Approve the 10% first-year support fee discount but require Novus to sign a standard amendment that documents acceptance criteria for the FHIR adapter and rollback plan. Legal to manage the amendment template.
4) Marcus to own technical delivery, including resource assignment and verification with Novus staging.

Kimberly — you have my sign-off to communicate the concession to Novus with the conditions above. Please route the SOW amendment to Legal and copy me on the DocuSign.

Vivek
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0189
